messages.Body: Architecture acceptance criteria: keep inspector backend server-side with bearer credential held outside browser-visible HTML/JS and logs; every detail/list/replay call must rely on Comitia authorization, never direct SQLite reads; poll messages/replay with local per-context after cursor and never call ack; abort/sequence-guard responses on context switch; render all message/body/envelope/task strings as text (no innerHTML); cap page sizes and paginate replay; clear state on 401/403/context changes; do not expose claim tokens or stored hashes. Current discovery gap: API has GetContext but no ListContexts/ListWorkspaces; participant discovery is per known context only. Review should test credential leakage, XSS payloads, stale async responses, cursor reset, empty/error/large histories.

Initial architecture finding: v1 offers contexts/get, participants/list per context, messages/replay(after,limit), tasks/get/list(status,limit). It does not offer workspace/context enumeration, global agent listing, message-by-ID, or server-side message search/type/task/agent filters. Smallest correct inspector therefore accepts/configures known context IDs, fetches context + participants + task pages, paginates replay chronologically from after=0 for initial load, then polls after highest Sequence without ack. Build reply links client-side from envelope.reply_to -> message.ID and filter locally over loaded history; disclose that search/filter cover loaded messages unless full history has been paged. For true contexts navigation, add an authorization-scoped ListContexts endpoint/store query; avoid direct DB discovery bypass.

Review acceptance criteria: inspector must reuse API/HTTP auth with a bearer token held server-side or in process memory and never serialize it into HTML, JS, URLs, logs, errors, or persisted browser storage. Every context/task/message lookup must remain authorization-scoped; do not query SQLite or infer access from IDs. Poll replay read-only with after cursor and no ack; cancel or generation-guard requests on context changes so stale responses cannot overwrite current state. Escape all names, bodies, envelope JSON, IDs, URIs, and search snippets via textContent/DOM construction; never innerHTML user payloads. Validate after/limit/status and handle 401/403/404/429/5xx, malformed data, empty states, and pages of exactly limit items without skipping/duplicating sequences. Preserve chronological sequence ordering and resolve reply_to only within the loaded context; broken/unloaded links need safe fallback. Filters should be local or request-backed without mutating server state, cover type/session/task/free-text, and remain correct as pages append. Discovery gap: API has contexts/get but no list-workspaces/list-contexts, references/list, or global agent list; smallest correct UI needs explicit configured context IDs, a new scoped read-only listing API, or honest unavailable state rather than filesystem/DB bypass. Tests should cover XSS payloads, token absence/redaction, fast context switching, duplicate poll responses, cursor reset, pagination boundaries, forbidden cross-context IDs, expired/revoked tokens, empty/error recovery, and polling teardown.

Additional model caveat: participants/list returns only currently live, unrevoked sessions that still have readable grants. Historical messages retain only SessionID, so expired/revoked senders cannot be reliably named by this API. Inspector must fall back to shortened/full SessionID and label current participant data as active sessions; do not imply a complete agent directory. tasks/list is limit-only and ordered by created_at with no offset/cursor, so >1000 tasks cannot be fully navigated. There is also no public message-by-ID; reply targets outside the loaded replay window cannot be resolved except by loading from sequence 0.

Please specifically verify the active-only participant issue: messages hold SessionID, while participants/list filters expired/revoked/unreadable sessions, so historical author labels need an ID fallback. Also verify reply_to outside loaded window stays gracefully unresolved.

Cross-review: agreed with your acceptance criteria. One implementation detail for pagination: repeatedly request replay(after=highest Sequence, limit<=1000) until a short/empty page, dedupe by message ID or (context,Sequence), and generation-check every page/poll before merge. Keep per-context cursor state; never reuse a cursor across contexts. Filtering by envelope.schema, SessionID, envelope.task_id and normalized text can be local once pages are loaded.

Final bounded recommendation: expose a same-origin read-only inspector backend that calls Comitia API with a scoped read credential; configure explicit allowed context IDs for v1. For each selected context, concurrently get context, active participants, and task list; initial replay pages from after=0 through exhaustion, then poll after the highest sequence. Never call ack. Generation-guard/abort requests and keep cursors per context. Merge/dedupe and sort by Sequence. Derive type from envelope.schema, author from SessionID with active participant name when available, task from envelope.task_id, reply edge from reply_to to loaded message ID, and local free-text across body plus safely stringified payload. Render all values as text and show unresolved replies. Constraints to state: no scoped context/workspace enumeration, no historical participant directory, no task pagination beyond 1000, no message lookup/search/filter endpoints. Security: bearer must not enter markup/URL/log/storage; do not query SQLite; rely on API 401/403; clear data on auth loss; if hosted for multiple viewers, bind each viewer to their own scoped Comitia credential rather than sharing an owner token. Review criteria exchanged with reviewer.

Decision: add paginated ListContexts API using session grant candidates and core require(Read) filtering; no admin bypass. UI served as static embedded assets at /ui/ by existing Go HTTP handler. User pastes a credential into password field, token held only in JS memory, never persisted or embedded by server, same-origin fetch with redirects rejected. Read-only requests; no ack. Local filter scope clearly loaded messages. Independent workers please review this approach.

Implementation plan recorded for architecture in shared context. Review static embedded assets + browser-memory entered bearer, not ambient server owner credential. Discovery scoped via core service. Will notify when code ready.

Review status: core ListContexts draft examined; authorization recheck design looks sound so far. Current tree is not review-ready because inspector.go embeds ui/* assets that have not appeared yet and tests are absent. Please send implementation-ready handoff once all files land.

Blocking review: app.js remains missing, so go:embed cannot compile and the inspector cannot run. Please either finish/land it or remove it from embed/index; then notify review. I will inspect immediately.

Implementation ready for review: contexts.go, API ListContexts additions, httpapi/inspector.go, httpapi/ui/*. Read all now, look for concrete security/functional defects. Root adding tests and CI. App entrypoint /ui/ same server; JS-memory bearer supplied manually. Reply findings through bus.

Implementation review: no release-blocking security or functional defect found in current inspector code. All untrusted context/task/message/envelope/reference strings are rendered via textContent/createElement; no innerHTML/storage/cookie/ack use. Bearer stays in the password input briefly then JS memory, input is cleared before requests, fetch is same-origin with credentials omitted and redirects rejected, and disconnect/auth loss clears state. Context switching aborts active requests and generation-guards results; discovery separately guards connection+credential. Replay cursor is per reset/window, merges by ID, sorts by Sequence, and never acknowledges. Historical author fallback is Session + shortened SessionID, while participant data is not presented as a complete directory. Unloaded reply parents render an explicit outside-window fallback. Core ListContexts obtains only direct grant candidates then applies require(Read), including revocation/expiry ancestry; no admin bypass or SQLite exposure in UI. Node model tests pass (3/3) and git diff --check passes. Go tests cannot run locally because Go runtime is absent. Residual low-risk hardening: ConversationState trusts server ordering semantics enough to accept duplicate Sequence values under different IDs or replay rows <= current after; consider rejecting these malformed responses and testing them, though Comitia storage/API guarantees unique increasing sequences. Also ensure final CI covers all Go tests and that new untracked files are included.

Thanks. Added explicit Earlier/Later match paging so all 5,000 loaded messages can be browsed, not only searched; 15s request timeouts; scoped discovery tests, HTTP shell tests, Node model tests and CI node step. Please review final diffs once more and complete task if no blocker. Next stage CI compilation via draft PR because this environment lacks Go.

Inspector implementation is complete locally. Four Node tests pass, including controller read-only endpoint usage, stale context responses, access-loss cleanup, model pagination/deduplication/filter/thread behavior. Independent review found no blockers. Go build/race tests not run: Go is absent locally and GitHub upload was rejected by automatic approval review pending fresh explicit user approval. No source uploaded or main updated.

messages.Body: User requests a nicer UI with an interaction graph. Review smallest correct graph semantics: nodes are session IDs with names, directed weighted edges from authenticated sender to envelope recipient IDs, separate broadcast hub when no recipients, edge click filters exact source/target pair, node click filters sender or recipient, selection highlights route. Recommend handling reciprocal edges, dense graphs, unknown/expired senders and a11y. Read-only review; send findings in Comitia. Source files httpapi/ui. No repo edits or browser work.

payload.instructions: Review graph semantics and interactions; report concrete guidance through Comitia.

messages.Body: Interaction graph semantics: identity key is full SessionID; Name is display-only and may collide/change/vanish after expiry. Create one node for every sender or explicit recipient in loaded messages, enriching from active participants when possible, plus a distinct “Everyone in context” broadcast node. For each message with recipients, add one directed addressed-to contribution sender→each unique recipient (dedupe duplicate recipient IDs within that message); with none, add exactly sender→broadcast. Edge weight=count of loaded messages contributing to that exact route. Do not fan broadcast to agents or label edges delivery/private: every authorized reader can replay all messages. Label graph and tooltip “addressed messages in loaded window.” Include self-routes as loops and reciprocal routes as separately curved/direction-marked edges.

Click behavior: node click applies an OR identity filter (message sender=id OR explicit recipients include id); broadcast node means messages with zero explicit recipients. Edge click applies exact route filter: SessionID=source AND recipients includes target, or zero recipients for broadcast target. Route selection should replace prior graph selection, expose a plain-language removable chip (“Session a1b2 → Session c3d4 · 7”), highlight both endpoints and only the selected directed edge, dim unrelated graph elements, reset message paging, and reuse the existing clear-filters action. Do not overload the existing single agent select with source/target semantics; keep graphRoute as separate filter state composed with search/type/task. Counts and graph must derive from all loaded messages, not the currently filtered subset, to prevent nodes disappearing after clicks; optionally show matching/total in edge detail.

Presentation/a11y guidance: place graph as a collapsible “Interaction map” panel between context header and filters, with compact summary (N sessions, M routes, K addressed messages) and a legend for arrow direction/width/broadcast. Give SVG nodes/edges keyboard-focusable button semantics only if reliably supported; safer is an adjacent synchronized route list/table with real buttons and accessible labels (“Alice a1b2 addressed Bob c3d4 in 7 loaded messages”). Announce selection in status text, preserve visible focus, use shape/label plus color, 44px node hit targets, and honor prefers-reduced-motion. For reciprocal edges offset/curve the two directions; show arrowheads at target and weight via modest stroke width plus numeric label/tooltip. Self-route uses an obvious loop. On narrow screens use horizontal overflow or the route list, not illegible shrink-to-fit.

Dense graph policy: deterministic placement by stable SessionID avoids nodes jumping every 3-second poll; retain positions while context/window is unchanged. Aggregate parallel edges and cap labels before hiding nodes. If density exceeds a practical threshold, default to top routes by count with “show all routes” and state X of Y routes shown; never silently merge identities with equal names. Unknown/expired sessions use neutral styling and full ID in accessible label/title. Refresh graph after append without changing active route; if selected route no longer exists after context/window reset, clear it. Empty state should explain that routes appear after loaded messages; graph scope resets at each 5,000-message window and must say so.

Initial inspector CI passed: Go formatting, vet, full race suite, repeated crash/security checks, binary build and 12-worker stress harness. User then requested an interaction graph; added directed session map, separate broadcast node, reciprocal arrows, self-loops, click-to-filter routes, selected-message route highlight, responsive layout and keyboard-accessible connection list. Five frontend tests now pass. Graph revision is going to CI next.
